items.title: fix(signal): retain case-sensitive link destinations (#151754)
items.summary: fix(signal): retain case-sensitive link destinations (#151754) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes missing destination URLs in Signal replies when a displayed URL differs from its HTTP(S) target only by path, query, or fragment case, such as `[example.com/Report](https://example.com/report)`. ## User Impact Signal messages, chunked replies, and media captions retain the authored destination instead of displaying only the differently cased label. Existing scheme/domain, `www.`, trailing-slash, and mailto deduplication remains intact; no configuration change is needed. Preserving the suffix also makes percent-escape spelling differences visible: `%2f` versus `%2F` can now produce a redundant destination suffix even though the escapes represent the same byte. This change does not introduce URL canonicalization. ## Why This Change Was Made Signal's duplicate-link comparison lowercased the entire URL before the shared Markdown renderer could preserve the destination. The comparison now preserves HTTP suffix case while continuing to normalize the host. Existing shared rendering still owns destination expansion, chunk sizing, and style offsets. The original contributor commit is preserved. Focused regressions now live in the existing formatter suites instead of a second HTTP recorder suite; existing media-access tests retain transport and attachment coverage. ## Evidence An isolated Linux/arm64 run exercised the registered `pnpm openclaw message send` CLI and the public Signal send API through the actual native HTTP client. Only the external signal-cli daemon was replaced by a loopback JSON-RPC recorder; no internal formatter or transport was mocked. - All 15 CLI/API scenarios passed on the candidate. The baseline lost path-, query-, and fragment-case destinations; the candidate retained them. - Chunked messages respected the configured limit and preserved UTF-16 style offsets after supplementary characters. A PDF caption preserved five style kinds and the exact 607-byte attachment. Account and recipient routing were asserted on actual `POST /api/v1/rpc` requests. - Plain-mode passthrough and existing normalization controls passed; the percent-escape spelling difference above was explicitly observed. - Focused candidate tests: **75 passed across 3 files**. The same formatter regressions against the baseline produced **5 failures / 43 passes**. Scoped lint reported **0 warnings / 0 errors**, and formatting passed. For example, the recorded wire text changed from `example.com#Install` to `example.com#Install (https://example.com#install)`. **Source scope:** these results cover baseline `bef4c20d45bdd23c3557eb71962f908c691a7ed6` plus this PR's formatter repair and focused regressions. The proof retains a pre-existing main-only golden test that is intentionally not added by this PR. These results are not a full historical-branch or hosted-CI result. The formatter SHA-256 is `c950ee86d4d814dfbe7f6ed7e81126db874dbf4db480104b3057e4a5b143b58b`. **Live-proof limit:** this proves the OpenClaw-to-signal-cli payload boundary, not real Signal recipient delivery, client rendering, link tapping, or PDF display. The previous review and author follow-up requested real Signal setup evidence. That requirement is not claimed complete or waived: fresh review must judge the explicitly bounded evidence under the repository's channel-boundary proof policy. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.summary: fix(install): fall back to portable Node after package manager failure (#134386) Windows installations can now recover automatically when winget, Chocolatey, or Scoop fails or leaves an unsupported Node.js runtime. Guarded package-manager attempts warn and continue through the remaining methods to the existing elevation-free portable Node installer. Runtime validation still gates OpenClaw installation. The installer remains the sole owner of runtime provisioning. Updated Windows documentation and regression coverage describe and protect failure fallthrough, successful recovery, and final refusal when no usable runtime can be provisioned. Validation: all 99 exact-head checks completed without failures, including Windows installer CI and openclaw/ci-gate. The isolated Windows recovery trace exercised real portable download, extraction, PATH recovery, and runtime/SQLite validation after an injected Chocolatey failure. Codex review was scoped-clean; ClawSweeper reported no actionable findings or Rank-up moves. Related: #133869
